But they also knew there was something else in the pond, something big and green and scary. It was an alligator, and their mom and dad told them to stay away from it.

One day, Ben and Lily saw a mysterious box near the pond. It was shiny and red and had a bow on it. They wondered what was inside. Maybe it was a toy or a cake or a surprise. They ran to the box and opened it. But instead of something nice, they saw a big sign that said "BOO!" and a loud noise that made them jump.

They were so scared that they dropped the box and ran back to the pond. They did not see the alligator that was hiding under the water, waiting for them. The alligator saw them and opened its mouth. It was hungry and wanted to eat them.

"Help, help!" Ben and Lily cried. "There is an alligator!"

Their mom and dad heard them and came running. They saw the alligator and grabbed Ben and Lily and pulled them away from the pond. They were safe, but they were also very sorry.

"We are sorry, mom and dad," Ben and Lily said. "We should have listened to you and stayed away from the pond and the alligator. We should not have been curious about the mysterious box. It was a bad joke and we learned our lesson."

Mom and dad hugged them and said, "We are glad you are okay, Ben and Lily. We love you very much. But you have to be careful and obey us. The pond and the alligator are dangerous and the mysterious box was a trap. Next time, do not go near them or you might get hurt."

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "We will, mom and dad. We will." They went home with their mom and dad and never played near the pond or the alligator or the mysterious box again. They learned that curiosity can be good, but it can also be bad. They learned to be smart and safe and listen to their parents.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play in the garden. One day, they find a big rock. It is brown and hard.

"Look, Tom, a rock!" Mia says.

"Can we take it home?" Tom asks.

Mia tries to lift the rock, but it is too heavy. She asks Tom to help her. They both pull and push, but the rock does not move.

"Maybe it is stuck in the ground," Mia says.

"Maybe it is magic," Tom says.

They look at the rock more closely. They see some shiny bits on it. They are different colors: red, green, blue.

"What are these?" Mia wonders.

"They are minerals," Tom says. He remembers what their mom told them. "Minerals are parts of rocks. They are very old and pretty."

"I want one," Mia says. She reaches for a blue mineral. She tries to break it off the rock, but it is too hard.

"Ow, it hurts!" she cries.

Tom reaches for a red mineral. He tries to break it off the rock, but it is too hard.

"Ow, it hurts!" he cries.

They look at each other. They have scratches on their fingers.

"Maybe we should leave the rock alone," Mia says.

"Maybe we should," Tom agrees.

They run back to their mom. She gives them a hug and a band-aid. She tells them to be careful with rocks.

"They are old and hard. They can hurt you," she says.

Tom and Mia nod. They still think the rock is magic, but they do not touch it again. They play with their toys instead.

Lily turned around and saw him. She was not scared. She was angry.

"I'm sorry, Lily," he said. "I thought it was a clever place to hide. I wanted to reveal myself and make you laugh."

"It's okay, Tom," she said. "But next time, hide in a better place. A place that is fun and colorful and exciting. Like the swings, or the sandbox, or the merry-go-round."

The moral of the story is: Do not act like an ostrich, or you might get your head stuck in a bucket of paint.

Lily rides her bike slowly and carefully. She looks at the flowers and the birds. She smiles and enjoys the ride. Ben rides his bike fast and recklessly. He does not look at the flowers and the birds. He only looks at his bike and how fast he can go.

He sees a big hill and thinks, "I want to go down that hill. It will be fun and exciting." He does not see the sign that says, "Danger. Do not go down this hill." He does not see the rocks and the holes on the hill. He does not see Lily on the path below the hill.

He speeds down the hill, feeling the wind in his hair. He laughs and shouts, "Whee! This is awesome!" He does not hear Lily's voice, saying, "Ben, stop! It's dangerous!" He does not see Lily's face, full of fear and worry.

He crashes into Lily, knocking her off her bike. They both fall to the ground, hurting themselves. Their bikes are broken and twisted. They cry and scream. Mom runs to them, scared and angry. She hugs them and checks if they are OK. She says, "Ben, what have you done? You were careless and foolish. You could have hurt yourself and your sister badly. You did not listen to me. You did not follow the rules. You are in big trouble, young man."

Ben feels sorry and ashamed. He says, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I was stupid. I did not mean to hurt you. Please forgive me."

Lily is hurt and sad. She says, "Ben, you were silly and mean. You did not care about me. You only cared about yourself. You made me scared and angry. You broke my bike and my heart."

Mom says, "Lily, I know you are upset. But Ben is your brother. He loves you and he is sorry. He made a mistake and he learned his lesson. Can you forgive him and give him a hug?"

Lily thinks for a moment. She loves her brother, too. She knows he is not always bad. She says, "OK, mom. I forgive you, Ben. But you have to be more careful and kind. And you have to help me fix my bike and your bike."

Ben says, "Thank you, Lily. I will be more careful and kind. And I will help you fix our bikes. I'm sorry I was careless and I speeded. I love you, sister."

They hug each other and say sorry again. Mom smiles and says, "I love you, both. Now let's go home and clean your wounds and your bikes. And remember, no more speeding and no more carelessness."

One day, Sam and Ben see a new horse in the stable. It is brown and white and has a long mane. The farmer says, "This is Spot. He is a stubborn horse. He does not like to do what I tell him. He only likes to run and jump."

Sam and Ben want to ride Spot. They ask the farmer, "Can we ride Spot, please?"

The farmer says, "No, you cannot. Spot is too wild for you. He might buck you off or run away. You can ride the other horses. They are gentle and calm."

Sam and Ben are sad. They think Spot is beautiful and fun. They want to make friends with him. They say, "Please, let us try. We will be careful and gentle. We will not make him angry or scared. Maybe he will like us and listen to us."

The farmer says, "All right, but only for a little while. And only if I watch you. You have to wear helmets and hold the reins tight. And if Spot does anything bad, you have to get off him right away."

Sam and Ben are happy. They put on helmets and climb on Spot. They stroke his neck and say, "Hello, Spot. We are Sam and Ben. We want to play with you. We will not hurt you or make you do things you do not like. We will be nice to you. What is your name?"

Spot looks at them with his big eyes. He snorts and shakes his head. He does not answer. He does not care about their names. He does not want to play with them. He wants to run and jump. He is a stubborn horse. He kicks his legs and starts to run. He runs out of the stable and into the field. He jumps over the fence and the stream. He does not stop or slow down.

Sam and Ben are scared. They hold on to the reins and the saddle. They try to make Spot stop or turn. They say, "Spot, stop! Spot, come back! Spot, listen to us!"

But Spot does not stop or come back or listen. He does what he wants. He is a stubborn horse. He runs and runs and runs.

Ben and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to cook something for Mom and Dad. They found some eggs, bread, cheese and jam. They also found a colorful tie that Dad left on the table.

"Let's make a sandwich with cheese and jam," said Ben. "And we can put the tie on it to make it pretty."

"OK," said Lily. "But how do we cook the eggs?"

Ben thought for a moment. He remembered that Mom sometimes put eggs in a pot with water on the stove. He decided to try that. He filled the pot with water and put two eggs in it. Then he turned on the stove.

"Look, Lily, the water is bubbling," he said. "That means the eggs are cooking."

Lily nodded. She took two slices of bread and spread cheese and jam on them. Then she put them together to make a sandwich. She looked for a knife to cut it, but she couldn't find one. She decided to use her hands instead. She tore the sandwich in half and put one half on a plate. Then she took the colorful tie and wrapped it around the sandwich like a ribbon.

"Wow, Lily, that looks nice," said Ben. "But we need another plate for the other half."

He looked around and saw a big plate on the counter. He reached for it, but it was too high. He climbed on a chair to get it, but he lost his balance and fell. The plate crashed to the floor and broke into pieces.

"Ben, are you OK?" Lily asked.

Ben felt a pain in his arm. He started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow," he said. "My arm hurts."

Mom and Dad heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. They saw the mess and the crying Ben. They were shocked and worried.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

"We wanted to cook something for you," Lily said. "But we made a big oopsie."

Mom and Dad hugged Ben and Lily. They checked Ben's arm and saw that it was bruised, but not broken. They cleaned up the broken plate and the water on the stove. They thanked Ben and Lily for their sweet idea, but they also explained that cooking was not a safe game for little kids. They said they should always ask for help before using the stove or the knife.

They also saw the sandwich with the tie on it. They smiled and said it was very colorful and creative. They asked Ben and Lily if they wanted to share it with them.

Ben and Lily nodded. They were happy that Mom and Dad were not angry. They ate the sandwich together and agreed that it was yummy. They also promised to be more careful next time. They gave Mom and Dad a big hug and a kiss. They said they loved them very much.

She left the room and closed the door.

Tim and Sam looked at each other and shrugged. They did not want to clean their toys. They wanted to play with them. They picked up their favorite toys and started to play.

They did not notice that their mom had left a figure on the door. It was a figure of a fairy. She had a wand and a smile. She was watching them.

The fairy waited for a while and then said, "Hello, boys. I am the fairy of toys. I have come to see how you treat your toys."

Tim and Sam paused. They looked at the figure on the door. They were surprised and scared.

They said, "Who are you? How can you talk? What do you want?"

The fairy said, "I am here to teach you a lesson. You have been very bad to your toys. You have not cleaned them or cared for them. You have made them filthy and unhappy. You do not deserve them."

Tim and Sam said, "No, no, please, don't take our toys. We love them. We will clean them. We will be good."

The fairy said, "Sorry, boys, but you have to learn your lesson. Goodbye."

The fairy smiled and said, "That's what you get for being bad to your toys. Maybe one day, you will be good again and I will turn you back. But until then, you will stay as toys. Goodbye."

She flew away and left the room.

The moral of the story is: You should take care of your toys and keep them clean. If you don't, you might lose them or worse. You should be grateful for what you have and share it with others. You should be kind and respectful to your toys and to your mom.

Suddenly, Fred's dad shouted, "Woah! Look at this hill!" Fred was feeling scared, so he asked "Are we gonna make it?" His dad replied, "Yes, of course we can!". So, his dad began to pull the wagon up the hill with all his strength.

At the top of the hill, Fred felt so proud and happy that they had made it. When they got back home, Fred's dad patted him on the head and said, "Good job, Fred! Our lively ride was a lot of fun today".

The happy stone began to roll around with joy and dance in the grass. It was no longer tired - it was energized! The stone bounced and skipped and sang, until it was so tired again. Its energy had left it and it surrendered once more to its tiredness.

The little stone went to sleep in the grass, dreaming of feeling energized again. The end!

One night, Lily saw a bright star in the sky. She pointed at it and said, "I want that star! Give me that star!"

Her mom and dad looked at her and shook their heads. "You can't have that star, Lily. That star is very far away and belongs to everyone. You can only look at it and make a wish."

Lily did not listen. She stamped her feet and said, "No! I want that star! It is mine! Mine! Mine!"

Her mom and dad sighed and took her to her room. They tucked her in and said, "Good night, Lily. We love you, but you need to learn to share and be grateful. Maybe tomorrow you will be nicer."

Lily did not say good night. She turned away and closed her eyes. She was still angry and wanted the star.

But as she fell asleep, she had a dream. She dreamed that she flew to the star and grabbed it. She was very happy and said, "Ha! I have the star! It is mine! Mine! Mine!"

But then, the star spoke to her. It said, "Hello, Lily. Do you know my name?"

Lily was surprised and scared. She said, "No, I don't know your name. Why do you talk?"

The star said, "I talk because I am alive. I have feelings and thoughts, just like you. My name is Stella, and I have many friends in the sky. We shine and dance and sing together. We make people happy and hopeful. But you took me away from them. You are very selfish and spoiled, Lily. You don't care about anyone but yourself."

Lily felt ashamed and sad. She said, "I'm sorry, Stella. I didn't know you were alive. I didn't know you had friends. I was wrong to take you. Please forgive me."

Stella said, "I forgive you, Lily. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will be kind and generous from now on. You have to share and be grateful for what you have. You have to love and respect others, even if they are different from you. Can you do that, Lily?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, Stella. I can do that. I will do that. Thank you for teaching me a lesson."

Stella smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. Now, let me go back to the sky. You can still see me and wish on me, but you can't have me. I belong to everyone."

Lily let go of Stella and watched her fly away. She felt a warm glow in her heart. She said, "Goodbye, Stella. I will remember you and your words. You are a very nice star."

Stella winked at her and said, "Goodbye, Lily. You are a very brave girl. I hope you have sweet dreams."

Days turned into weeks, and soon the seed grew into a beautiful plant with a graceful stem and leaves. And then one day, Lily saw something amazing. A tiny cup was growing on the plant! She was so happy and proud that she had grown her very own cup. 

From that day on, Lily knew that even when things break, she could always grow something new and beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck who loved to play in the water. One day, he went to the pond and saw a big frog. The frog was weird because he had a needle on his head. The little duck didn't know what to do, so he decided to splash water on the frog. 

The frog didn't like it and tried to jump away, but the needle got stuck in a branch. The little duck felt bad, so he asked his friends for help. They all came and pulled the frog out of the branch. The frog was happy and thanked the little duck and his friends. 

From that day on, the little duck and the frog became friends and played together in the pond. They would splash each other and have lots of fun. The little duck never forgot about the weird needle on the frog's head, but he didn't care because he had a new friend. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved boats. He saw a big navy boat in the harbor and wanted to go inside. He asked the captain if he could enter the boat, but the captain said it was too noisy and dangerous for a little boy like him. 

Timmy was sad and went home. He told his mom about the big navy boat and how he couldn't enter. His mom told him not to worry and that they could watch the boat from afar. 

The next day, Timmy snuck out of the house and went back to the harbor. He climbed over the fence and snuck onto the navy boat. He was so excited to be inside, but then he heard someone coming. It was the captain! 

The captain was angry and told Timmy to leave immediately. Timmy was so scared that he fell and hurt himself. He had to go to the hospital and his mom was very upset with him for disobeying her. From that day on, Timmy learned to always listen to his mom and never enter places he wasn't supposed to.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to bake with her mommy in the kitchen. One day, they were making cookies in the oven. Lily's mommy told her to be careful because the oven was hot.

Lily was fascinated and said, "I want to make everything shine like the oven!" 

Her mommy smiled and said, "You can make things shine by keeping them clean and smooth, just like the oven."

His mom said, "You can eat your banana after you clean up your room."

The moral of the story is that cleaning up can lead to finding things that glow, like a flashlight. And it's important to listen to your mom and clean up your messy room before doing anything else.

Timmy said, "Let's solve this problem. We can use this stick to make a bridge." 

Spot was happy and ran across the bridge to get the bone. But as he was chewing on the bone, he accidentally swallowed it whole. Spot started to feel sick and had to go to the vet. 

The vet said, "I'm sorry, but Spot can't eat bone. It's dangerous. Spot is very sick." 

Timmy was sad and cried because he loved Spot so much. Spot was very sick and couldn't play anymore. They never tried to cross the river again.

Suddenly, Benny saw a sneaky fox trying to steal the bag of carrots. Benny knew he had to be brave, so he hopped over to the fox and said, "Stop! That's not your bag, it belongs to someone else!" The fox was surprised and ran away.

Benny was so happy that he saved the bag of carrots. He decided to share them with all his friends in the forest. From that day on, Benny wasn't so shy anymore. He felt proud of himself for doing the right thing.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They were having fun.

But then they saw a big, scary animal in the bushes. It had spots and sharp teeth. It was a leopard! The leopard was hungry and wanted to eat them.

Lily and Ben started to panic. They screamed and ran away from the leopard. They dropped their ball and did not look back.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "There is a leopard in the park!"

A man heard them and came to see what was wrong. He saw the leopard and grabbed a stick. He waved the stick at the leopard and made loud noises. The leopard was afraid and ran away.

The man was a zookeeper. He had been looking for the leopard. It had escaped from the zoo. He was sorry that it scared Lily and Ben.

He took them to his car and drove them to their home. He gave them their ball and a hug. He said he was sorry again.

Lily and Ben were safe and happy. They thanked the zookeeper and said goodbye. They went inside their home and told their mom what happened. They were very brave.

Their mom was proud of them. She gave them a snack and a kiss. She said they could play in the park again, but only when the leopard was back in the zoo.

Lily and Ben agreed. They did not want to see the leopard again. They also did not like being dirty. They had mud and grass on their clothes and shoes. They needed a bath. They hoped their ball was not too dirty either. They liked their ball. It was their favorite toy.

Lily and Max were twins who lived on a big ranch with many animals. They liked to play with the horses, the cows, the chickens and the dogs. But they did not like to play with each other. They always fought and ignored each other.

One day, their mom told them to go to the barn and feed the animals. Lily and Max did not want to work together. They each took a bucket of food and went to different sides of the barn. Lily fed the horses and the cows, and Max fed the chickens and the dogs. They did not talk or look at each other.

But then, something bad happened. A big storm came and the wind blew hard. The barn door slammed shut and locked. Lily and Max were trapped inside the barn with the animals. They tried to open the door, but it was too heavy and stuck. They shouted for help, but no one heard them. They were scared and cold.

"Lily, I'm sorry I ignored you," Max said. "I don't like to fight with you. You are my sister and I love you."

"Max, I'm sorry I ignored you, too," Lily said. "I don't like to fight with you, either. You are my brother and I love you."

They hugged each other and felt better. Then they had an idea. They asked the animals to help them. The horses and the cows pushed the door with their noses. The chickens and the dogs scratched the door with their claws. The animals were strong and flexible. They worked together and opened the door.

Lily and Max ran out of the barn and saw their mom waiting for them. She was happy and relieved to see them. She hugged them and praised the animals.

"Lily and Max, I'm so proud of you," she said. "You learned to work together and to be kind to each other. And you made friends with the animals. They saved you from the storm. You are lucky to have them on our ranch."

Lily and Max smiled and thanked the animals. They petted them and gave them more food. They also thanked their mom and said they were sorry for being mean. They promised to play nicely and not ignore each other anymore. They learned a big lesson that day. They realized that they were not alone on the ranch. They had each other and the animals. They were a family.

"Maybe it is a lion!" Sam says. He is brave and curious.

"Maybe it is a snake!" Ben says. He is scared and careful.

They go closer to the cage and look inside. They see a small bird. It is gray and sad. It has no water or food. It does not sing.

"Hello, bird!" Sam says. He wants to be its friend.

"Go away, boys!" the bird says. It does not want to talk.

"Why are you in the cage?" Ben asks. He feels sorry for the bird.

"Someone put me here a long time ago. They forgot about me. They never let me out. They never gave me anything to wear. I am cold and lonely." the bird says.

"That is not fair!" Sam says. He is angry and kind.

"We can help you!" Ben says. He is smart and gentle.

They run to the house and get a blanket, a bowl, and some seeds. They come back to the cage and open the door. They wrap the blanket around the bird and give it the bowl and the seeds.

"Thank you, boys!" the bird says. It feels warm and happy. It starts to sing.

Lily woke up and felt hungry. She went to the kitchen and saw her mom. "Mom, can I have cereal?" she asked.

"Sure, honey. What kind of cereal do you want?" her mom said.

Lily looked at the boxes on the shelf. She saw one with a picture of a bear and honey. She liked honey. It was sweet. "I want that one, mom. The bear cereal," she said.

"Okay, here you go. Do you want some milk with it?" her mom said.

"Yes, please. Milk makes cereal yummy," Lily said.

Her mom poured some milk into a bowl and added some cereal. She gave it to Lily and a spoon. Lily sat at the table and started to eat. She tasted the cereal and smiled. It was crunchy and sweet. She liked it a lot. She ate some more and said, "Thank you, mom. This is good cereal."

"You're welcome, sweetie. I'm glad you like it. Do you want some more?" her mom said.

Lily looked at her bowl. It was almost empty. She was still hungry. She nodded and said, "Yes, please. More cereal, mom."

"Good job, Lily. You ate well. Do you want to help me wash the dishes?" her mom said.

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I like to help. Let's wash the dishes." She got off her chair and took her bowl and spoon to the sink. Her mom followed her and they washed the dishes together. Lily felt proud and happy. She loved her mom and her cereal.

Lily was an intelligent girl who liked to count everything. She counted her fingers, her toes, her dolls, and her books. She also liked to count the forks in the kitchen drawer. She would take them out one by one and say the numbers out loud.

One day, her mom asked her to help set the table for dinner. She gave Lily a pile of forks and told her to put one on each plate. Lily was happy to help. She started to count the forks as she placed them on the table.

"One, two, three, four, five, six," she said. She looked at the table and saw that there were six plates, but seven forks. She had one extra fork. She wondered what to do with it.

She decided to ask her mom. She walked to the kitchen and said, "Mom, I have a problem. I have seven forks, but only six plates. What should I do with the extra fork?"

Her mom smiled and said, "That's very good, Lily. You are very intelligent to notice that. The extra fork is for me. I need two forks because I am going to eat salad and pasta. Can you bring me the extra fork, please?"

Lily nodded and said, "Oh, I see. Yes, I can bring you the extra fork. Here you go, mom." She handed her mom the fork and said, "I like to count forks. It is fun."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I like that you like to count forks. It is fun and it helps you learn. You are a very smart and helpful girl, Lily. I love you."

Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, mom." She went back to the table and waited for dinner. She was proud of herself for counting the forks and solving the problem. She thought that counting was a very intelligent thing to do.

Sara and Tom are playing in the park. They see a big, old tree with many apples. Sara says, "Let's pick some apples and taste them. They look yummy." Tom nods and climbs the tree. He picks a red apple and throws it to Sara. Sara catches it and takes a bite.

"Mmm, this apple is sweet and juicy," Sara says. "Do you want to try?" She offers the apple to Tom. Tom shakes his head. He says, "No, thank you. I have a green apple. It is sour and crunchy. I like it better." He bites his apple and makes a funny face.

Sara laughs and says, "You are silly, Tom. Sour apples make your nose wrinkle. Sweet apples make you smile. Here, have another bite of mine. Maybe you will change your mind." She holds the apple closer to Tom.

Tom looks at the apple and says, "OK, I will try. But only a little bit." He takes a small bite and chews. He says, "Hmm, this apple is not bad. It is sweet and juicy. But I still like my green apple more. It is sour and crunchy. It makes me feel awake."

Sara smiles and says, "That's OK, Tom. We can like different things. That's what makes us friends. We can share our apples and enjoy them together." She takes another bite of her apple and says, "These apples are the best. They are from the old tree. The old tree knows how to grow good apples."

Tom nods and says, "Yes, these apples are the best. They are from the old tree. The old tree is our friend. It gives us apples and shade and fun. We should thank the old tree." He takes another bite of his apple and says, "Thank you, old tree. You are the best."

But the bull was smart. He smelled Lily and followed her. He saw the barn and pushed the door. He made a loud noise and the animals woke up. They saw the bull and were afraid. They ran away or hid. The bull looked for Lily and saw the hay. He charged at the hay and threw it away.

Lily screamed and cried. She had no place to go. The bull was angry and came closer. He lowered his horns and got ready to hit her. Lily closed her eyes and wished it was a dream. But it was not a dream. It was real.

The bull hit Lily and hurt her. Lily felt pain and blood. She stopped screaming and crying. She stopped breathing and living. The bull snorted and walked away. He was not ashamed. He was proud. He had won. Lily had lost. She would never dream again.

Lily liked to draw with her crayons. She had many colors, but her favorite was white. She liked to draw white things on white paper, like snowflakes, clouds, and stars. She thought they were perfect and beautiful.

One day, her friend Max came over to play. He saw Lily's drawings and was confused. "What are these?" he asked. "I can't see anything."

Lily smiled and said, "They are white things. They are very pretty. You have to look close."

Max looked closer, but he still could not see anything. He shook his head and said, "No, they are not pretty. They are boring. You should use other colors, like red, or blue, or green. They are more fun."

They climbed and climbed, and found many different rocks. Some were smooth, some were rough, some were shiny, some were dull. They picked up some rocks and put them in their pockets.

Then they saw something very bright. It was a rock that looked like the sun. It was gold! They had never seen a gold rock before. They were very excited and wanted to take it home.

But the gold rock was very heavy. Lily and Max could not lift it. They tried to push it, but it did not move. They looked at each other and did not know what to do.

They had to decide. Should they leave the gold rock and go back to mom, or should they stay and try to get the gold rock? They thought hard.

They remembered that mom was waiting for them. They remembered that they had many other rocks in their pockets. They remembered that they were hungry and thirsty. They remembered that they loved mom more than gold.

They decided to leave the gold rock and go back to mom. They said goodbye to the gold rock and thanked it for being so pretty. They ran down the hill and found mom.

Mom hugged them and asked them what they found. They showed her their rocks and told her about the gold rock. Mom smiled and said they were very smart and brave to make that decision.

They went home and had a snack. They put their rocks in a box and looked at them. They felt comfortable and happy. They had a good day.

Tom and Anna wanted to make a pumpkin pie for their mom. They went to the garden and looked for a big pumpkin. They saw many pumpkins, but some were too small, some were too green, and some had bugs on them. They kept looking until they found a wide pumpkin that was orange and round.

"Look, Anna, this is the one!" Tom said, pointing to the wide pumpkin.

"Yes, it is perfect!" Anna said, smiling. "But how can we get it? It is too heavy for us."

Tom had an idea. He ran to the shed and got a wagon. He brought it to the pumpkin and said, "Help me, Anna. We can put the pumpkin on the wagon and pull it to the house."

Anna nodded and helped Tom. They pushed and lifted the pumpkin onto the wagon. It was hard work, but they did it. They pulled the wagon to the house, where their mom was waiting.

"Wow, what a nice pumpkin!" their mom said, surprised. "Did you find it in the garden?"

"Yes, we did, mom!" Tom and Anna said together. "We want to make a pumpkin pie for you!"

"That is so sweet of you!" their mom said, hugging them. "Thank you, my loves. You are very clever and strong. You succeeded in finding the best pumpkin for the pie. Now let's go to the kitchen and make it together."

Sara and Ben are playing in the kitchen. They have a big pot and some spoons. They pretend to cook soup.

"What do you want to put in the soup?" Sara asks Ben.

"Beef!" Ben replies. He likes beef. He has a toy cow that he calls Beefy.

"Okay, beef it is!" Sara says. She pretends to cut some beef and put it in the pot. She stirs the soup with a spoon.

"Can I taste it?" Ben asks. He is hungry.

"Sure, but be careful. It is hot!" Sara warns him. She gives him a spoonful of soup.

Ben blows on the soup and puts it in his mouth. He makes a face.

"Yuck! This soup is not good!" He says. He spits out the soup.

"Why not? What is wrong with it?" Sara asks. She is confused.

"It is too white!" Ben says. He does not like white soup. He likes red soup with tomatoes.

"White soup is good too!" Sara says. She likes white soup with milk and cheese.

"No, it is not! It is bad!" Ben says. He does not want to eat any more soup.

They start to argue. They do not agree on the soup.

Mom hears them and comes to the kitchen. She sees the mess they have made.

"What are you doing?" She asks them.

"We are making soup!" Sara and Ben reply together.

Mom smiles. She knows they are just playing. She helps them clean up the kitchen.

"Maybe next time you can make soup that you both like," She says.

"Okay, Mom," Sara and Ben say. They hug Mom and say sorry for the mess.

They go to the living room and play with Beefy. They are happy again.

Tim is sad and angry. He loves his lizard. He thinks Rex is beautiful and fun. He says, "No, Rex is not a monster. He is a lizard. He is my friend. He is not gross. He is cool. You are mean. You don't know anything about lizards. Go away."

Sam is mad too. He thinks Tim is silly and weird. He says, "Fine, I will go away. You are a baby. You play with lizards. You are not cool. You are boring. I don't want to be your friend."

Sam leaves Tim's room. He goes to the living room. He finds his mom. He says, "Mom, can we go home? I don't like Tim. He has a lizard. He is a baby."

Tim stays in his room. He hugs Rex. He says, "Rex, you are my friend. You are not a monster. You are a lizard. You are cool. I like you."

One day, they saw a man coming out of the mill. He was angry and had a stick in his hand. He shouted at them, "Go away! This is my mill! You are making too much noise!"

Anna and Ben were frightened. They ran away from the mill and hid behind a tree. They heard the man shut the door of the mill with a loud bang. They looked at each other and whispered, "Who is he? Why is he so mean?"

They decided to go back to their home and tell their mom what happened. They hoped the man would not come out of the mill again. They did not want to play near the mill anymore. They wanted to play somewhere else, where they could have fun and be safe.

The police came and took Lily and Tom to the station. They called their parents. Their parents were very mad. They scolded them and grounded them. Lily and Tom lost their friendship. They never played together again. They were sad.

Anna and Ben nod and wipe their tears. They go to the garden with mom and find a spot for Fluffy. They take a shovel and dig a hole. They gently lift Fluffy and put him in the hole. Lila was a little fish who loved to explore the sea. She liked to swim fast and see new things. One day, she saw a big, shiny thing that looked like a rock. She wanted to go closer and touch it.

But her friend Nemo, a small shrimp, said, "No, Lila, that is not a rock. That is a trap. It has a hole with food inside, but if you go in, you cannot come out. It is for catching fish like us. We should stay away from it."

Lila did not listen to Nemo. She said, "You are just scared, Nemo. I am not afraid of anything. I want to see what is inside the trap. Maybe there is something fun or tasty. You can follow me or stay here."

Lila swam towards the trap, and Nemo followed her. He did not want to leave her alone. He hoped she would change her mind and come back. But Lila was too curious and stubborn. She went inside the hole and saw some worms and shells. She thought they looked yummy and started to eat them.

Suddenly, she heard a loud snap. The trap closed and Lila was trapped. She tried to push and bite the bars, but they were too strong. She realized she had made a big mistake. She was scared and sorry. She wished she had listened to Nemo.

Nemo saw what happened and felt sad and worried. He wanted to help Lila, but he did not know how. He saw a big shadow above the trap. It was an enormous shark. The shark smelled the fish in the trap and wanted to eat them. He opened his mouth and bit the trap.

Lila screamed and Nemo hid behind a coral. The shark shook the trap and broke it. He swallowed Lila and the worms and shells. He did not see Nemo, who was too small and fast. Nemo escaped and swam away. He was safe, but he lost his friend.

Nemo learned a lesson that day. He learned that some things are dangerous and not worth exploring. He learned that he should listen to his friends who care about him and warn him. He learned that he should be careful and smart in the sea. He missed Lila and hoped she was happy in the shark's belly. He wished she had learned the lesson too.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, Tom has a new toy. It is a mighty robot. It can walk, talk and shoot lasers.

"Look at my robot!" Tom says to Sue. "It is very cool and strong. Do you want to play with it?"

Sue nods. She likes robots too. She takes the robot and makes it walk and talk. She has fun.

"Can I have a turn?" Tom asks. He wants to play with his robot too.

Sue shakes her head. She does not want to give it back. She likes the robot too much. She hugs it and says, "No, it is mine now. Go away!"

Tom feels sad and angry. He wants his robot back. He says, "That is not fair! It is my robot! Give it back or I will not be your friend!"

Sue does not care. She says, "I do not need you. I have the robot. It is my friend now. Go away!"

Tom runs away. He cries. He feels lonely. He goes to his house. He sees his mom. She is making tea. She has a mug. It has a picture of a robot on it.

"Mom, can I have some tea?" Tom asks. He hopes it will make him feel better.

"Of course, my dear," his mom says. She sees his tears. She asks, "What is wrong? Why are you crying?"

Tom tells her what happened. He tells her about Sue and the robot. He tells her how Sue was mean and did not share.

His mom hugs him. She says, "I am sorry, Tom. That was not nice of Sue. She should have shared with you. Sharing is caring. Maybe she will realize her mistake and say sorry to you."

Tom hopes so. He says, "Maybe. But I do not want to play with her anymore. She is not a good friend."

His mom says, "I understand. But maybe you can give her another chance. Maybe you can invite her to have tea with us. Maybe you can show her your mug. Maybe you can teach her how to be a good friend."

Tom thinks about it. He says, "Maybe. But only if she gives me back my robot."

His mom smiles. She says, "That sounds fair. Why don't you call her and see if she wants to come over?"

Tom nods. He picks up the phone. He calls Sue. He says, "Hi, Sue. Do you want to have tea with me and my mom? I have a mug with a robot on it. It is very cool. And I will let you play with my robot again. If you say sorry and share."

Sue is surprised. She feels sorry. She says, "Yes, Tom. I want to have tea with you and your mom. I am sorry for being mean. I will give you back your robot. And I will share. You are a good friend."

Tom smiles. He says, "OK, Sue. Come over soon. I will wait for you."

He hangs up the phone. He tells his mom. His mom says, "Well done, Tom. You are a mighty and kind boy. I am proud of you."

Tom feels happy. He hugs his mom. He says, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

They wait for Sue. They have tea and cookies. They play with the robot. They have fun. They are friends again.

Tom and Lily were twins who loved to go to the beach. They liked to play in the sand, splash in the water, and look for shells. One day, they saw a big whale on the shore. It was not moving and looked very sad.

"Look, a whale!" Tom said. "Can we touch it?"

"No, we can't," Lily said. "It is hurt and needs help. We have to find someone who can help it."

They ran to find their mom and dad, who were sitting on a blanket. They told them about the whale and asked them to come. Their mom and dad followed them to the shore, where they saw the whale.

"Oh, poor thing," their mom said. "It must have got lost and stranded by the tide. We have to call the animal rescue team. They will know what to do."

She took out her phone and called the number. Soon, a big truck and a boat arrived. The animal rescue team had a big net and a crane. They put the net around the whale and lifted it with the crane. They put the whale on the boat and took it to the water.

"Bye, whale," Tom and Lily said. "We hope you feel better and find your family."

The whale made a loud noise and waved its tail. It looked happy and grateful. It swam away into the deep water.

Tom and Lily learned that day that some animals need help when they are in trouble. They also learned that they should not touch or bother them, but remain calm and find someone who can help them. They felt proud and happy that they helped the whale. They also felt amazed and curious about the big and beautiful animal. They decided to learn more about whales and how to protect them. They also thanked their mom and dad and the animal rescue team for their help. They had a very special day at the beach.

One day, she went to the zoo with her mom and dad. She saw many animals, but she was not happy. She wanted to touch them and play with them. She did not listen to the signs that said "Do not feed" or "Do not climb". She demanded to go inside the cages.

Her mom and dad said no, that was dangerous and rude. But Lily did not care. She waited until they were not looking and sneaked into the cage of a big lion. She thought the lion was cute and fluffy. She wanted to hug him and take him home.

But the lion did not like Lily. He did not like her loud voice and her grabbing hands. He roared and showed his teeth. He was angry and scared. He wanted to escape from the cage and from Lily.

Lily was afraid too. She realized she made a big mistake. She screamed and cried for help. Her mom and dad heard her and ran to the cage. They saw the lion and Lily. They were terrified and called the zookeepers.

The zookeepers came and used a big net to catch the lion. They took him away to a safe place. They were angry at Lily and her parents. They said Lily could have been hurt or killed by the lion. They said Lily was lucky to be alive. They said Lily and her parents had to leave the zoo and never come back.

Lily was sad and ashamed. She wished she had listened to her mom and dad. She wished she had been nice and respectful to the animals. She learned a hard lesson. She was not proud of herself.

The moral of the story is: Do not demand things that are not yours. Do not ignore the rules and the warnings. Do not bother the animals that are not your friends. Be grateful and polite to everyone.

"Yes, Mom. But the naughty bird hurt us," Lily said.

"Thank you, Ben. Your fish is beautiful too. It looks like it can dive in the water." Lily said.

"Ooh, that looks fun. Can I try?" Ben asked.

"Sure, Ben. But be careful, don't hit your head on the sidewalk." Lily said.

Ben nodded and bent his knees and jumped forward, pretending to dive. But he jumped too far and his head hit the edge of the sidewalk. He felt a sharp pain and started to cry.

The lady heard Lily and saw Ben. She came over and looked at his wound.

"Yes, we were playing with chalk and he tried to dive and he hit his head." Lily explained.

She gave Ben and Lily their chalk and walked them back to the sidewalk. She waved goodbye and went back to her dog.

"Lily, I'm glad you're my friend. You helped me a lot." Ben said.

He tried to open the acorn, but it was too hard. He pulled and twisted, but it didn't budge.

"Maybe we need something to help us," Sara said. "Like a tool."

She looked around and saw a big stick. She ran to get it and brought it back to Ben.

"Here, Ben, use this stick," she said. "Maybe you can zip the acorn open with it."

Ben took the stick and tapped the acorn with it. Nothing happened. He tapped harder and harder, until he hit the acorn with all his strength.

CRACK!

The acorn split open and something flew out of it. It was a small, furry creature with a long tail and a black mask. It was a squirrel!

The squirrel was very scared and angry. It had been sleeping inside the acorn, and now it was awake and out in the open. It saw Ben and Sara and made a loud noise.

"SQUEAK!" it said.

Ben and Sara were very surprised and scared too. They dropped the stick and the acorn and ran away.

The squirrel chased them for a while, then stopped and went back to the acorn. It picked up the two halves and tried to put them back together. But it was too late. The acorn was broken and the squirrel had no home.

The squirrel sighed and looked for another acorn. It hoped it would find one that was big and shiny and had a little hat. And it hoped that no one would try to zip it open again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and chase each other. They saw a cricket on the grass. It was brown and shiny and made a loud noise.

"Look, a cricket!" Tom said. "Let's catch it and keep it as a pet."

Lily nodded. She liked animals. She ran after the cricket and tried to grab it with her hand. But the cricket was fast and jumped away.

"Wait for me!" Tom said. He followed Lily and the cricket. They ran across the garden, past the flowers and the trees and the pond.

They came to a big pile of dirt. It was dirty and smelly and had worms and bugs in it. The cricket jumped into the dirt and hid.

"Ha, I see it!" Tom said. He reached into the dirt and felt the cricket. He pulled it out and held it in his hand. It was dirty and wet and squirmed.

"Yuck, it's dirty!" Lily said. She wrinkled her nose. "I don't want it as a pet anymore. Let's throw it away."

Tom shook his head. He liked the cricket. He wanted to keep it. He put it in his pocket.

"No, it's mine!" he said. "I caught it. It's my pet. I will name it Chirpy."

Lily was angry. She wanted to share the cricket. She did not like Tom being selfish. She pushed Tom and tried to take the cricket from his pocket.

"Give it to me!" she said. "It's not fair. You have to share."

Tom pushed Lily back. He did not want to share the cricket. He wanted to keep it for himself. He ran away from Lily.

"Go away!" he said. "It's my cricket. You can't have it."

Lily ran after Tom. She was crying. She wanted to play with the cricket. She wanted to be friends with Tom. She did not understand why he was so mean.

They ran and ran and ran. They did not see where they were going. They did not see the road. They did not see the car. They did not hear the horn.

The car hit them. They fell to the ground. They did not get up. They did not move. They did not breathe.

The cricket crawled out of Tom's pocket. It was still alive. It jumped away and disappeared.

The end.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toy trucks in the yard. They had a big pile of sand and some rocks to load on their trucks. Tom had a red truck and Lily had a blue one.

"Look, I can load more sand than you!" Tom said, scooping up a lot of sand with his shovel. He dumped it on his truck, making it very heavy.

"That's not fair, Tom! You are taking too much sand!" Lily said, frowning. She only had a little sand on her truck. She wanted to load more, but Tom was being selfish.

"No, I'm not! It's my sand, I found it first!" Tom said, grabbing another shovel of sand. He did not care about Lily's feelings. He only wanted to have the biggest load.

Lily felt sad and angry. She did not like playing with Tom anymore. She had an idea. She waited until Tom was not looking, and then she took a big rock from the pile. She walked over to Tom's truck and put the rock on it.

"Hey, what are you doing?" Tom shouted, seeing Lily. He tried to move his truck, but it was too heavy. The rock was too big for his truck. It made his truck tip over and spill all the sand.

"Ha, ha! Now you have no sand!" Lily said, laughing. She felt happy. She had taught Tom a lesson.

Tom felt mad and sad. He had lost all his sand. He realized he had been selfish and mean to Lily. He wished he had shared the sand with her.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. Can we be friends again?" Tom said, looking at Lily.

Lily looked at Tom. She saw he was sorry. She decided to forgive him.

"Okay, Tom. I'm sorry, too. I should not have put the rock on your truck. Can we share the sand and the rocks?" Lily said, smiling.

"Sure, Lily. Let's share. We can have more fun that way." Tom said, smiling back.

They hugged and made up. They loaded their trucks with sand and rocks, but not too much. They measured their loads with a ruler. They made sure they had the same amount of inches. They played happily together. They learned to be kind and not selfish.

As time went by, the happy ball and the bird had many fun days in the wood. They laughed, played, and rolled around together. And they lived happily ever after in the small wood.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a big dream. He wanted to bring an enormous star down from the sky. Tim told his mom about his dream. "Mom, I want to bring a huge star from the sky," he said. His mom smiled and said, "One day, you will, my dear."

One day, Tim went to the park to play with his friends. While they were playing, they saw a big, bright star in the sky. Tim remembered his dream and told his friends, "I want to bring that enormous star down for us to play with!" His friends laughed, but they all thought it would be fun to try.

The next day, Tim and his friends found a long, strong rope. They tied one end to a tree and held the other end. Together, they threw the rope high into the sky. They tried and tried, but they couldn't reach the enormous star. Then, a kind bird saw them and wanted to help. The bird took the rope in its beak and flew up to the sky.

The bird tied the rope around the enormous star and flew back down. Tim and his friends pulled and pulled on the rope. Slowly, the enormous star came down from the sky. They were so happy! They played with the star all day long. When it was time to go home, they thanked the kind bird and let the star go back into the sky.

From that day on, every time Tim and his friends saw the enormous star in the sky, they remembered their fun adventure. And Tim knew that dreams can come true if you believe and work together with your friends.

Jack thought for a moment and said, "Let's guess how many times the sun will come out from behind the clouds today."

Lily thought that sounded fun, but she said, "That's difficult. I don't know how to guess."

Jack said, "It's easy. Just close your eyes and think really hard about how many times you think the sun will come out. Then, we'll count together and see who was closest."

They counted together and the sun came out six times! Jack was closest, but they both had a lot of fun guessing.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the sea with his mom and dad. He liked to swim and play in the water. He saw many fish and shells, but he wanted to see a dolphin. He asked his mom and dad, "Where are the dolphins? I want to see a dolphin!"

His mom and dad said, "Dolphins are very smart and friendly, but they are shy. They do not like to come near people. You have to be patient and quiet, and maybe they will show up."

Tom nodded and waited. He looked around the sea, but he did not see any dolphins. He felt sad and bored. He said, "I do not want to wait anymore. I want to see a dolphin now!"

He started to splash and yell in the water. He did not listen to his mom and dad, who told him to stop. He made a lot of noise and scared the fish and shells away.

Suddenly, he saw a black fin in the water. He thought it was a dolphin. He was very happy and excited. He said, "Look, look, a dolphin! I see a dolphin!"

He swam towards the black fin, but he did not know that it was not a dolphin. It was a shark. The shark saw Tom and opened its big mouth. It wanted to eat Tom.

Tom was very scared and screamed. He tried to swim away, but the shark was faster. He thought he was going to die.

But then, he heard a loud splash and a whistle. He saw a gray fin in the water. It was a dolphin. The dolphin saw Tom and the shark. The dolphin was very brave and strong. It hit the shark with its tail and made it go away.

Tom was very relieved and grateful. He said, "Thank you, thank you, dolphin! You saved me!"

The dolphin smiled and nodded. It said, "You are welcome, Tom. But you should not be so noisy and rude in the sea. You should respect the sea and its creatures. They are not here for your fun. They are here to live and be free. If you want to see dolphins, you have to be patient and quiet, and maybe they will show up."

Tom felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "I am sorry, dolphin. You are right. I was wrong. I will be patient and quiet, and respect the sea and its creatures. I hope you will forgive me."

The dolphin said, "I forgive you, Tom. You are a good boy. You learned your lesson. I hope you will remember it. Goodbye, Tom. Take care."

The dolphin waved its fin and swam away. Tom waved back and said, "Goodbye, dolphin. Thank you. Take care."

Tom swam back to his mom and dad, who hugged him and kissed him. They were very happy and proud of him. They said, "We are glad you are safe, Tom. We are proud of you. You saw a dolphin, and you learned a valuable lesson. You should always be patient and quiet, and respect the sea and its creatures. They are not here for your fun. They are here to live and be free."

Tom nodded and smiled. He said, "I know, mom and dad. I know. I love you, and I love the sea and its creatures. They are amazing and wonderful. I will never forget them, or the dolphin who saved me."

The end.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. They had a ball, a bike and a kite. They had fun with their toys, but they also liked to look at the animals in the pond. There were ducks, frogs and fish. And there was a big crocodile.

The crocodile was green and scaly. He had a long mouth with many teeth. He liked to swim in the water and sunbathe on the shore. But he was not happy. He was envious of the boys and their toys. He wanted to play with them, but he did not know how to ask.

One day, the boys were flying their kite near the pond. The kite was red and blue and had a long tail. It soared high in the sky and made the boys laugh. The crocodile watched them and felt sad. He wished he had a kite too.

He decided to try to get the kite. He waited until the boys were not looking and sprang out of the water. He snapped his jaws at the kite's tail and pulled it down. He thought he had caught the kite, but he only had a piece of cloth in his mouth.

The boys heard the splash and turned around. They saw the crocodile with their kite's tail and were scared. They ran away from the pond and shouted for help. The crocodile realized he had made a mistake. He had scared the boys and ruined their kite. He felt sorry and ashamed.

He spat out the kite's tail and swam back to the water. He hoped the boys would forgive him and come back to the park. He learned that being envious was not good. He decided to be happy with what he had and to be friendly to the boys and the other animals. He hoped they would be his friends too.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play outside, but today it is very cold. Mom says they have to wear hats and coats and gloves. Tom and Sam do not like that. They want to wear shorts and T-shirts.

"Let's go to the park anyway," Tom says. "We can order ice cream from the truck."

Sam thinks that is a bad idea. He says, "Ice cream is for hot days, not cold days. We will get sick if we eat ice cream now."

But Tom does not listen. He says, "You are a baby. I am a big boy. I can eat whatever I want."

They go to the park. They see the ice cream truck. Tom runs to the truck and orders a big cone. Sam stays away. He is cold and hungry.

Tom eats his ice cream. He feels happy for a moment. But then he feels very cold. He shivers and his teeth chatter. He also feels a pain in his throat. He coughs and sneezes.

He goes to Sam and says, "I don't feel good. I want to go home."

Sam says, "I told you so. You should have listened to me and Mom. Ice cream is not good for cold days. You have to eat warm and healthy food."

They go home. Mom sees Tom and says, "What happened to you? You look sick."

Tom says, "I ate ice cream at the park. It was cold and I wanted to be a big boy."

Mom says, "That was not a smart thing to do. You have to be careful with what you eat. You have to listen to your body and your family. They know what is best for you."

She gives Tom some soup and a blanket. She says, "Next time, order something else. Or better yet, stay home and play with your toys. It is too cold to go outside."

Tom says, "I'm sorry, Mom. I learned my lesson. I will listen to you and Sam from now on."

He hugs Mom and Sam. He feels warm and loved. He falls asleep on the couch.

The end.

Moral: Listen to your body and your family. They know what is best for you.

Anna and Ben were surprised and scared. They did not know there were fairies in the forest.

"Who are you?" Anna asked.

Flora said.

"Why not?" Ben asked. "It is just a mushroom. We like mushrooms. We want to have fun with it."

Flora shook her head. "It is not just a mushroom. It is a living thing. It has feelings and needs. It grows and changes. It gives us shade and food. It is our friend. You should not take what is not yours. You should respect other living things. That is what wise people do."

Anna and Ben thought about what Flora said. They realized she was right. They did not want to make the fairies angry and sad. They did not want to hurt the mushroom. They wanted to be wise.

"Sorry, Flora," Anna said. "We did not know. We will not pick the mushroom. We will leave it alone."

Anna and Ben nodded. They said goodbye to Flora and the mushroom. They ran back to their home. They told their mom and dad what they saw and learned in the forest. They were proud of themselves. They had made a new friend and a wise choice.

"What is match?" Tom asked. He followed his sister and sat down next to her.

"Wow!" Tom said. He reached for a match too. He wanted to try the game.

"Be careful, Tom. Matches are hot and can hurt you. You have to hold them away from your face and your clothes. And you have to blow them out before they reach the teaspoon. Or they will burn it and make a big mess." Jenny warned.

"OK, Jenny. I will be careful." Tom said. He copied his sister and lit a match. He tried to make it fit in the teaspoon. He blew it out just in time.

"Good job, Tom! You did it!" Jenny praised. She clapped her hands and smiled.

"Thank you, Jenny! This is fun!" Tom said. He smiled back and picked up another match.

"Sorry, Mom. We were bored and we wanted to play match. It is a game where you light the matches and try to make them fit in the teaspoon. It is very fun and exciting!" Jenny said.

"Fun and exciting? It is very silly and reckless! You are lucky you did not hurt yourselves or the house. You are both in big trouble. Give me the matches and the teaspoon right now. And go to your rooms. No more games for you today." Mom said.

Once upon a time there was a gray rock in a field. The rock was big and round, and it was the only one around.
One day a little ant came by and it decided to serve the rock. The ant pushed and prodded the rock and soon it began to move. The ant used all its might to push the rock and the rock kept moving until it came to a stop at the edge of the field.
The rock was now serving the ant and all the other animals in the field. It served as a place to rest, it served as a place to hide, and it even served as shelter from the rain.
The rock served different animals for many years, until one day a boy came and took the rock away, never to be seen again.
But the rock was never forgotten. The animals still remembered how it served them for so many years.

Timmy felt sad because he wanted to be the best at playing with swords. "I wish I had a bigger sword," Timmy said. 

"I know where we can get a bigger sword," Billy mentioned. "There's a big competition in the forest tomorrow. The winner gets a really big sword!" 

Timmy was excited to hear this and they both went to bed dreaming about the competition. The next day, they went to the forest and saw lots of other kids with their swords. The competition was very hard and Timmy tried his best, but he didn't win. 

Timmy felt sad and disappointed. He wished he had won the big sword. As they were walking home, they saw a sign that said "Beware of the dragon." They didn't pay attention to it and kept walking. Suddenly, they saw a big dragon in front of them! They tried to use their swords to fight the dragon, but it was too big and strong. 

Timmy and Billy realized they should have paid attention to the sign and not been so competitive. They learned that it's not always about winning, but about being safe and careful.

Tommy said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to do that."

Lily replied, "It's okay, Tommy. But now I can't drink my milk."

Tommy had an idea. He went to the kitchen and brought back a powerful blender. He put the broken glass and the milk in the blender and pressed a button. To Lily's surprise, the blender turned the glass and milk into a yummy milkshake.

Lily was so happy and said, "Thank you, Tommy! You are so smart."

Tommy smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you like it."

While they were still arguing, a kind lady heard them talking. She approached them and asked what was wrong. Juno and Sam explained their quarrel and the lady said she was happy to help them. She gave them each a pot of honey and told them to share it. 

Juno and Sam were very grateful and thanked the kind lady. After tasting the honey, they realised that it was the most delicious thing they had ever tasted. They quickly became friends again and agreed to never quarrel about silly things again. 

The moral of the story was that it is better to be grateful and share than to quarrel.

Jack and his dad were marching through the forest. It was a gloomy day and the trees looked like they were bowed down. The fog was thick and they couldn't see beyond the trees. Suddenly, a loud noise filled the air. Jack looked around and nudged his dad, but there was nothing to be seen. So, they kept marching. 

As they made their way further, the sound seemed to be getting louder. Nervously Jack asked his dad what it was, but he just patted Jack's shoulder and kept marching. Suddenly, a crack of light appeared through the trees, and the sound of music seemed to be coming from it.

Jack and his dad stopped to take a look. There in front of them stood a little band, playing away. The band members were all wearing bright clothes, waving their arms as they played, and the sound filled the forest all around. 

Jack grinned and took his dad's hand. Together, they marched towards the music and soon, their gloomy faces were filled with joy.

Tony then placed the toy car in front of the cricket and said, "Let's play a game, Rock! If I rock the car and it touches you, you have to move away one step, okay?" The cricket had no choice but to agree.

After a few moves, the cricket was about to win when all of a sudden, Tony said, "Stupid cricket! You're too slow!" The cricket was so angry that it jumped and hit the car, and Tony lost the game. The cricket flew away in anger, while Tony just sat on the ground sulking.

The knight was surprised and he said, "No, I will never give you my sword!"

The wizard grinned and he said, "I'm afraid you must give me your sword. Or I will turn you into a frog!"

The knight knew he had no choice, so he reluctantly handed over his sword to the wizard. The wizard laughed and he said, "Goodbye, brave knight. You will never see your sword again!"

The wizard left the knight all alone in the dark cave. The knight never saw his sword again and he was never able to go on any more adventures.

"Hello, Frosty!" Lily said. "You are our new friend."

"Yes, you are," Ben agreed. "But you look cold. Do you want a hug?"

They hugged Frosty and he smiled. But then they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck. It was coming fast. It was going to hit Frosty.

"Watch out, Frosty!" Lily shouted. "The truck is coming!"

"Run, Lily, run!" Ben yelled. "We have to get out of the way!"

They ran to the side of the road. But Frosty was still in the middle. The truck was getting closer. Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want Frosty to get hurt.

"Help, help!" they cried. "Someone, please help Frosty!"

Then they saw a man. He was wearing a blue uniform. He had a badge and a whistle. He was a police officer. He saw the truck and Frosty. He blew his whistle and waved his hand. He stopped the truck.

"Stop, stop!" he said. "You can't drive here. This is a no-truck zone. You have to follow the order."

The truck driver was sorry. He did not see Frosty. He did not mean to hurt him. He said he was sorry and backed up. He drove away.

The police officer walked to Frosty. He checked him. He was okay. He did not lose his nose or his eyes. He did not break his hat or his scarf. He was still smiling.

"You are a lucky snowman," the police officer said. "You have two good friends. They love you very much. They tried to rescue you."

Lily and Ben ran to Frosty. They hugged him again. They thanked the police officer. They were happy. Frosty was safe.

"Thank you, thank you!" they said. "You are a hero. You saved Frosty."

The police officer smiled. He was glad. He liked to help people. And snowmen.

"You are welcome, welcome," he said. "But now you have to go home. It is getting dark. And icy. You don't want to catch a cold."

Lily and Ben nodded. They said goodbye to Frosty. They said they would come back tomorrow. They took their sled and went home. They held hands. They were warm. And happy.

Lily loved to bake with her mom. They made cakes, pies, and cookies. Lily liked to eat the sweet treats, but she also liked to share them with her friends. She was a kind and generous girl.

One day, Lily and her mom baked a big cake for a party. They decorated it with frosting, sprinkles, and olives. Lily thought the olives looked like eyes. She thought the cake was very attractive. She wanted to show it to her friends.

She asked her mom if she could take the cake to the park. Her mom said yes, but she told her to be careful and not to drop it. Lily promised to be careful. She put the cake in a box and carried it to the park.

At the park, she saw her friends playing. She called them and showed them the cake. They were amazed by the cake. They said it looked delicious and pretty. They asked Lily if they could have a slice. Lily said yes, but she asked them to wait. She wanted to find a table and some plates.

She looked around and saw a table under a tree. She walked towards it, holding the box. But she did not see a big rock on the ground. She tripped over the rock and fell. The box flew out of her hands and landed on the ground. The cake came out of the box and smashed on the grass. The frosting, sprinkles, and olives scattered everywhere.

Lily was very sad. She cried and cried. She had ruined the cake. She had nothing to share with her friends. She felt very bad.

Her friends ran to her and helped her up. They hugged her and comforted her. They told her it was okay. They said they did not care about the cake. They cared about her. They said she was their friend and they loved her. They said they could still have fun together.

The moral of the story is: Friendship is more important than things.

He snatched the red lollipop from them and ran away.

"OK, Tom, but be careful. The hill is steep and rocky," Lily says.

"Wow, look at the view, Lily! It's so pretty!" Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, it's amazing! I can see everything!" Lily says.

They sit on the grass and enjoy the view. They are proud of themselves for climbing the hill.

But then, they hear a loud noise. They turn around and see their ball rolling down the hill. It hits a rock and bounces off. It hits another rock and bounces again. It is going faster and faster.

"Oh no, our ball!" Tom and Lily shout.

They get up and run after the ball. They try to catch it, but it is too fast. They see the ball reach the bottom of the hill and cross the road. They see a car coming towards the ball.

"Stop, ball, stop!" Tom and Lily yell.

But the ball does not stop. It goes under the car and pops. It is broken.

Tom and Lily are sad. They love their ball. They cry and hug each other.

A man gets out of the car and sees the ball. He sees Tom and Lily on the hill. He feels sorry for them. He walks to them and gives them a new ball. It is red and shiny.

"I'm sorry, kids, I couldn't prevent your ball from breaking. Here, take this one. It's a gift from me," the man says.

They go back to the park and play with their new ball. They are careful not to lose it. They still like the view, but they like their ball more.

One day, a duck went to the mail box to see if he had any letters. He liked to get letters from his friends who lived far away. He hoped they would tell him about their adventures and send him pictures.

But when he opened the mail box, he saw only one letter. It was from a mean fox who lived in the woods. The letter said:

"Dear Duck,

I am very hungry and I want to eat you. I will come to your pond tomorrow and catch you. You cannot run or hide from me. You will be my dinner.

Your enemy, Fox."

The duck was very scared and sad. He did not want to be eaten by the fox. He did not know what to do. He ran to his best friend, a rabbit, and showed him the letter.

"Rabbit, rabbit, help me!" he quacked. "Look at this letter! The fox wants to eat me!"

The rabbit read the letter and frowned. He did not like the fox. He was very mean and cruel. He had a plan to help the duck.

"Don't worry, duck, I have an idea. We will trick the fox and make him go away. Come with me, we need some things."

The rabbit and the duck went to the garden and picked some carrots and lettuce. They also found some salt and pepper. They put them in a big basket and covered it with a cloth. Then they went back to the pond and waited for the fox.

The next day, the fox came to the pond. He saw the duck sitting on the shore, next to a basket. He licked his lips and smiled.

"Hello, duck, I'm here to eat you," he said.

"Hello, fox, I'm here to be eaten," the duck said. "But before you eat me, can I offer you something from my basket? It is a gift for you."

The fox was curious and greedy. He thought the basket might have something tasty and valuable. He agreed to look inside.

The duck opened the basket and showed him the carrots and lettuce. He said:

"These are for you, fox. They are very good and healthy. They will make you strong and smart. You should eat them first, before you eat me."

The fox did not like carrots and lettuce. He thought they were boring and bitter. He wanted to eat the duck, not the vegetables. But he did not want to be rude or suspicious. He decided to pretend to like them.

"Thank you, duck, you are very kind and generous. I will eat these first, before I eat you. They look very delicious and sweet."

He took a carrot and bit into it. But he did not know that the rabbit and the duck had sprinkled salt and pepper on the vegetables. The carrot was very salty and spicy. It burned his tongue and made him cough.

"Ah, ah, ah, what is this? This carrot is not sweet, it is bitter and hot! It hurts my mouth!" he cried.

He spit out the carrot and took a lettuce. He hoped it would be better. But it was not. It was also salty and spicy. It made him cough more.

"Ah, ah, ah, what is this? This lettuce is not good, it is bitter and hot too! It hurts my throat!" he cried.

He spit out the lettuce and looked at the duck. He was very angry and confused. He said:

"Duck, duck, what have you done? You have tricked me! You have given me bad food! You have made me sick!"

The duck smiled and said:

"Yes, fox, I have tricked you. I have given you bad food. I have made you sick. And now you cannot eat me. You should go away and leave me alone. You are not my friend, you are my enemy."

The fox realized he had been fooled. He felt very stupid and ashamed. He also felt very thirsty and sick. He did not want to eat the duck anymore. He wanted to drink some water and find some medicine. He ran away from the pond, coughing and sneezing.

The duck and the rabbit laughed and hugged. They were very happy and proud. They had saved the duck from the fox. They had used their brains and their courage. They had also used the mail and the vegetables. They were very good friends. They decided to write a letter to their other friends and tell them about their adventure. They hoped they would like it and send them some nice pictures.

Tom was sad and scared. He did not know what to do. He ran back to Sam's room. He gave the car to Sam.

"I'm sorry, Sam. I broke your car. The fire and the ash did it. I did not mean to," Tom said.

Sam looked at the car. He was angry and sad. He liked his car. It was his favorite car. He did not want to share it.

"You are a bad friend, Tom. You did not borrow my car. You ruined it. You did not listen to me. You are deaf. Go away. I don't want to play with you," Sam said.

Tom felt bad. He wanted to say sorry. He wanted to fix the car. He wanted to be friends with Sam. But Sam did not want to talk to him. He turned away and cried.

Tom left the room. He walked home. He was lonely and sorry. He wished he had been more careful. He wished he had not borrowed the car. He wished he had listened to Sam.

The little bird chirped back, "It's okay Princess. Just be more careful next time." 

The Princess felt bad for what she did and promised to always be more careful. She learned that it's important to think about others and not just herself. From that day on, she made sure to be kind to all the animals in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved animals, especially the ones he saw at the zoo. One day, Timmy and his mom went to the zoo. They saw lions, tigers, and bears, oh my! Timmy thought the monkeys were weird because they liked to swing and make funny faces.

When Timmy got home, he decided to study more about the animals he saw at the zoo. He looked at pictures and read books about them. Timmy learned that lions were very strong and tigers had stripes. He also learned that monkeys were very smart and could use tools like humans. Timmy was happy to learn new things and couldn't wait to go back to the zoo to see his animal friends again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls, especially her favorite doll, Sarah. Sarah was special because she had a beautiful leather dress.

One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. They were all eager to play together. But then, Lily and her best friend Emma started to quarrel over who would get to play with Sarah. Emma wanted to play with the doll, but Lily didn't want to share.

Later that day, Lily went home and put Sarah on her bed. She felt bad about the quarrel with Emma. Suddenly, she remembered something her mom had told her: "Sharing is caring."

The next day, Lily went back to the park and apologized to Emma. She even let Emma play with Sarah for a little while. Emma was so happy and they all had fun together. Lily realized that sharing was much more fun than quarreling. From then on, she always shared her toys with her friends.

As she continued her walk, she saw a ball on the ground. She picked it up and decided to kick it around. She kicked it so hard that it went flying into the bushes. She looked for it, but couldn't find it.

She felt happy and forgot all about the ball she had lost. From then on, Lily knew that sometimes, the best treasures are the ones that are hidden in plain sight.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and watch her favorite cartoons on TV. One day, she found a magic potion that made things shrink. 

Excitedly, she ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, look! I found a magic potion that can make things shrink!" 

Her mom was surprised and said, "Wow, that's incredible! But be careful, Lily. We don't want anything to get hurt." 

Lily nodded and decided to try the potion on her toy car. She poured a little bit on it and watched in amazement as it shrank to the size of her palm. 

She ran back to her mom and exclaimed, "Mommy, look! It worked! My car is so small now!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "That's amazing, Lily. But remember, magic potions can be dangerous. Let's put it away for now and play with your toys." 

Lily agreed and happily played with her shrunken car, feeling proud of herself for discovering something incredible.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little mouse named Max. Max lived in a big pumpkin in the garden. One day, Max was outside the pumpkin when he saw a big, scary cat coming towards him. 

Max ran back inside the pumpkin and shouted, "Help! Help! Someone listen to me!" 

His friend, a wise old owl, heard Max's cries and flew over to the pumpkin. "What's wrong, Max?" asked the owl. 

"A big, scary cat is trying to catch me!" said Max. The owl thought for a moment and then said, "I have an idea. Let's make a plan to trick the cat." 

Max and the owl worked together to make a clever plan. They put a piece of cheese outside the pumpkin and waited for the cat to come. When the cat came, Max and the owl jumped out and scared the cat away. From that day on, Max and the owl were the best of friends and always listened to each other.

"Hello little bird," said Lily. "Why are you in the forest?"

"I'm looking for my family," said the bird. "They flew away and I don't know where they went."

"Don't worry," said Lily. "I'll help you find them. Let's look together."

So, Lily and the little bird searched the forest together. They looked high and low, but they couldn't find the bird's family. Finally, they heard a chirping sound and followed it. It led them to a tree where the bird's family was waiting for them.

"Thank you for helping me," said the little bird. "I'm so happy to be back with my family."

Lily smiled and said, "I'm glad we found them. Now let's go home before we get too cold and start to shiver again."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet cat named Mittens. Mittens was very fluffy and loved to play with Lily. One day, Lily wanted to go outside to play with Mittens, but her mom said it was too distant and she had to stay inside. Lily was sad and started to cry. 

Mittens saw that Lily was upset and insisted on coming inside to see her. Lily was so happy to see Mittens and gave her a big hug. Mittens purred and licked Lily's face. 

From that day on, Lily and Mittens were the best of friends. Even though they couldn't always play outside, they had each other to keep them company. Mittens would always insist on being by Lily's side, and Lily loved her pet cat more than anything in the whole wide world. The end.

First, Remy hopped to his friend Sally the squirrel. "Sally, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Sally shook her head and replied, "No, Remy, I did not drop the carrot. I like nuts, not carrots." Remy thanked Sally and continued his search.

Next, Remy went to see his friend Benny the bird. "Benny, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Benny looked at the carrot and replied, "No, Remy, I did not drop the carrot. I like seeds, not carrots." Remy thanked Benny and hopped away. 

Finally, Remy found his friend Tommy the turtle. "Tommy, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Tommy smiled and replied, "Yes, Remy, I dropped the carrot. Thank you for finding it!" Remy gave the carrot back to Tommy, and they all played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Daisy. One day, Daisy decided to go on an adventure. As she gathered her things, she picked up a needle, which was her mom's. Her mom saw her doing this and said, "Daisy, why are you taking the needle?" Daisy responded, "I'm going to go on an adventure and I need it!" Her mom smiled and said, "That's not a good idea". Undeterred, Daisy gathered her things and set out.

On her adventure, Daisy saw many incredible things. She soon became thirsty and said, "A needle can't quench my thirst". She started to cry. Suddenly, an old man appeared. He said, "Daisy, don't cry. A needle can't help you in a situation like this. You need to think of what could help you!" Daisy thought for a moment, and then thought back to her mom's words. "Ah, I should have listened to my mom!", she said.

Joe was stuck and he started to panic. Luckily, a kind bird was flying nearby and quickly flew over to save Joe. The bird carefully carried Joe down the tree, letting him jump off when they were close to the ground.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Polly and Peter.

But Polly didn't listen and took the wire home.

Peter then said, "See? You shouldn't take things that don't belong to you or it will create problems."

One day, the brown frog asked, "Why do you hurry? We have all the time in the world!" The green frog said, "I hurry, because I want to touch everything that nature has to offer!" 

The brown frog paused for a bit and thought about it. Then he smiled and said, "That's a very great thing to do! I'm so excited and cannot wait to join you!" 

The two friends happily hopped together and experienced everything new and mysterious the nature had to offer. 

The moral of the story is that life is short, and that we should take the time to explore the beautiful world around us and experience the mysterious things it has to offer.

Grandmother and the little creature soon began doing yoga together. They did lots of stretches, poses and breathing exercises. After a while, the little creature was exhausted but thanked Grandmother for teaching her. Grandmother smiled and said, "You're welcome, little creature. That was fun!"
